main_body: Half-timbered house: a large hipped tile roof with a gable dormer over a plaster and timber front wall, plus a front porch with a door
top_band: The tiled roof slope fills rows 3-42 at x=36. It is drawn as a tile pattern alternating #804530 and #49252c, with lighter scallop highlights near the eave. A dark eave row sits at about rows 43-45, directly above the plaster wall.
evidence: The big roof slopes read as horizontal surfaces seen from above (hip, ridge and gable dormer), with a dark eave row beneath them. Below that sit the plaster and timber south walls and the porch. The doors and window have dark inner frames. This matches the building references, so the 3/4 contract is met. The column scan alternates between two roof tones because of the tile rows, not because of a front face.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours, against 185 and 66 in the references. It carries 3 colours per tile against 18 and 11, and its 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 17% against 0%. Its dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, where the references are 7-9%, so the outline is a near-black sticker line. Roof tiles are a two-tone stripe pattern with no per-tile highlights. The plaster walls are flat beige with no speckle, and the shading is far shallower than the references.
